_comment: BRIDGE-4 CAMPAIGN BUILD MANIFEST — ProgIR -> SenProg.
⛔⛔ READ THIS FILE AS YOUR BRIEF. The translator prompt names only this file, the worklist, the
Wavefront config and your worktree — it does NOT name AGENT-BRIEF.md, so anything written only
there never reaches you. That was measured on the bridge-3 campaign, where two agents ran a whole
batch against a SIBLING campaign's instructions because this file had been inherited unchanged.
The campaign ports C++ into an EXISTING Rust crate (crates/compiler/deeptools). There is no C
build, no shim to compile and no FFI boundary, so `configure` is a no-op and the C-side gates in
the translator playbook do not apply.
⛔ TRANSLATOR GATE — run EXACTLY these two, from the repo root, ONCE PER BATCH at the end:
cargo check -p deeptools
cargo test  -p deeptools
Never the workspace build, never the acceptance build: a worktree's target/ is ~6 GB and this
host has under 60 GB free. The orchestrator owns that gate.
═══ WHAT YOU ARE PORTING ═══
33 units, the transitive closure of SenProg EMISSION, across FOUR files — not one:
sys-arch-spec/dpc/dpc.cpp        3   (entry point Dpc::convertIr2Senprog at :615)
sys-arch-spec/progir/progir.cpp  6   (the operand text: OperandAttr::print at :25-62)
sys-arch-spec/progir/progir.h   18   ALL IN-CLASS definitions
sys-arch-spec/isa/isa.cpp        6
A .cpp-only scan would miss eighteen of the thirty-three.
AUTHORITY: /Users/nickm/git/deeptools-src/<file>:<line>  (revision a0d29abbed, what every banner
cites). ⛔ /Users/nickm/git/deeptools is a DIFFERENT revision — do not use it.
✅ THE EXTRACT crustify-bridge4/cpp/bridge4.cpp IS VERIFIED VERBATIM, 33 of 33, by
tools/verify_extract.py, which shares no code with the extractor: it re-derives each body's end
with its own scanner, compares length AND content, asserts brace depth reaches zero at the last
character, and never appends a brace. Both negative controls fail as required. Still CITE the
authority — bridge 2's extract was not checked this way and 366 of its 384 bodies were truncated,
because its check re-sliced the source with the same length the extractor used.
⭐ SENPROG IS A PRINT FORMAT. What is being ported is the exact TEXT: field order, spelling,
separators, and which fields are omitted. A function that decides WHAT to write without writing
it is not a port.
⛔ A CORELET IS A SINGLE CHARACTER HERE — dpc.cpp:638-639 is
`corelet = unitName.back(); unitName.pop_back();`, with L3LU/L3SU special-cased to "0" at
:635-636. Bridge 2's ExtendUnitNameToCorelet only ever writes 0 or 1, so a third corelet is
mislabelled at both ends of the ladder.
═══ HARD CAPS — MEASURED, NOT GUIDANCE ═══
Bridge 2's first 144 functions cost 43 HOURS of wall clock, 89% of it model time, 586 MILLION
cache-read tokens against 5 million output — 30 to 48 turns per function. Of 30,991 lines
produced, only 5,306 were implementation: 12,333 were doc comments and 12,575 were tests.
82% of the output was not the port. So, per ported function:
doc comment lines        8   — the `/// Replaces: eNNN_name` anchor, one line of what it
does, and any TRAP. Nothing else. NO TUTORIALS.
test functions           1   — or 2 where the vendor's own case plus one negative both apply
cargo check / test       once per BATCH, at the end — NOT per function
⛔ DO NOT RE-VERIFY CITATIONS. Take the file:line from crustify-bridge4/UNITS.tsv as given; the
review pass owns that check and re-measured every drifted citation on bridge 2.
⛔ DO NOT GREP THE CRATE TO DISCOVER TYPES. Your .rs home's header names what your units need.
If something is genuinely absent, add it and say so in the commit message.
⭐ NOT CAPPED: correctness, and the emission. Cutting the port to hit a cap is the one failure
worse than being slow.
═══ WHAT "PORTED" MEANS ═══
The WHOLE function, INCLUDING ITS EMISSION. A hand attempt on bridge 2 extracted each function's
decision rule into a documented predicate — is_l3(), BurstSetting::of(), Granularity::checked() —
left out the part that emits, and reported it done. Nothing called any of it. What may be dropped
is the mechanism for REACHING data; never what is written, in what order, with what separators.
If the island cannot express something, EXTEND THE ISLAND — deciding a function is unnecessary is
not the porter's call.
═══ CRATE RULES (crates/compiler/deeptools/CLAUDE.md) ═══
🛑 NEVER RUNTIME REFUSE: no Result, no Err(, no .ok_or, no assert!, no debug_assert!. A closed set
is an enum; an invariant is a type. `todo!` naming unported work is allowed.
⛔ NEWTYPES, never raw scalars — transposing two extents must be a type error.
⛔ NO STRINGS for closed sets.
⛔ Const-generic traits Arch / Model / Workload flow through.
This is a pure-logic port with no C left anywhere: no bindgen, no -sys, no ffi_export, no
extern "C", no Foo/FooRef/FooMut triple, no unsafe, no sanitizers — whatever the generic
C-porting conventions in your system prompt say about those.
